body.statement: If \(m_i=m\) for every \(i\), \(S=\{0,1\}\times\mathcal Z\), and \(|\alpha|=\gamma\), then \(Q_S=2u m^{K-\gamma}\) and \(Q_S-\kappa_0(S)-\eta(S)=\min\{Q_S,D_{K,m}(\gamma)\}\), where \(D_{K,m}(\gamma)=m^K+\sum_{j=K-\gamma+1}^K\binom Kj(m-1)^j+m^{K-\gamma}\). Thus the Hall frontier reduces exactly to \(D_{K,m}(\gamma)\ge Q_S\).
body.justification: This reduction checks that the support theorem contains the banked rectangular result rather than replacing it with an unrelated analogue.
body.gap: The prior proposal proves only this symmetric full-support boundary and explicitly leaves heterogeneous alphabets and structural zeros unresolved.
body.consumer: Existing full-support applications retain their arithmetic diagnostic, while sparse-support applications gain the strictly finer Hall certificate.
